chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

exercises.name: Place the capo
exercises.purpose: Clamp just behind the fret, straight across.

params.action: press firmly, all strings clear, no buzzing
params.cue: behind the metal, not on top of it

exercises.coaching: A capo is a clamp that shortens the strings. Put it just behind the 2nd fret, straight across, snug but not choking. Now your open chords sound higher.

exercises.name: G–D–Em–C with capo 2

params.cue: play the same shapes; the capo does the transposing

exercises.coaching: Capo on 2, play G-D-Em-C with the SAME shapes. It now sounds in A (A-E-F#m-D). You just played a song in a new key without learning new chords. That is the capo superpower.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: Can't hit the high notes? The capo lets you play the same easy shapes in any key. One clamp, and suddenly every song fits your voice.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Capo just behind the 2nd fret, straight and snug. It shortens the strings so your open chords sound higher. No new fingerings.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Capo on 2, play G-D-Em-C like always. It sounds in A now. Same shapes, new key — you can match any singer. That is the whole point.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: A capo means you never have to learn a song in an uncomfortable key. The shapes you already know travel anywhere.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Capo basics done. Lesson 15 we build raw change speed — the skill that makes everything feel easy.
